chunks: And ʿUmar ibn Yazīd narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:
If the believer dies, and forty men from among the believers attend his funeral and say: O Allah, we know nothing of him except good, and You know him better than we do,
Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: I have accepted your testimonies and forgiven him for what I know of that which you do not know.

key_terms.أَرْبَعُونَ: forty; the number of believers whose attendance is mentioned
key_terms.جَنَازَتَهُ: his funeral bier or funeral procession
key_terms.خَيْرًا: good; the good known of the deceased
key_terms.شَهَادَاتِكُمْ: your testimonies; the believers’ witness regarding the deceased
key_terms.غَفَرْتُ: I have forgiven; Allah’s granting of pardon
key_terms.لَا تَعْلَمُونَ: you do not know; what remains unknown to people but known to Allah
key_terms.ٱللَّهُمَّ: O Allah; opening word of supplication
key_terms.ٱلْمُؤْمِنُ: the believer; here, the deceased faithful person

ai.seo_question: What is the merit of forty believers attending a funeral and testifying to the goodness of the deceased?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that when a believing community bears good witness for a deceased believer, Allah accepts their testimony and grants forgiveness. It highlights the spiritual value of communal presence at the funeral and the importance of speaking well of the deceased with sincerity.
